note: Every MCP server adds tool definitions to the agent's context. Add only the servers you use. `eag mcp add <name>` previews by default and writes only with --yes, after backing up your mcp_config.json.

context7.description: Up-to-date library and framework documentation lookup (resolve a library, then query its docs).
context7.when: You work with fast-moving libraries and want current APIs instead of training-data guesses.

sequential-thinking.when: Long multi-step design or debugging sessions where explicit thought revision helps.

memory.description: Local knowledge-graph memory (entities, relations, observations) persisted to a JSON file.
memory.when: You want structured long-term memory in addition to EAG instincts and session summaries.

playwright.description: Browser automation through Playwright with accessibility-tree snapshots.
playwright.when: Scripted E2E exploration outside Antigravity's built-in browser, or in Gemini CLI.

chrome-devtools.description: Chrome DevTools for agents: performance traces, network, console, Lighthouse-style insights.
chrome-devtools.when: Diagnosing web performance (LCP/INP/CLS), network errors and console failures.

firebase.description: Firebase CLI MCP server (projects, apps, rules, deploy status). Antigravity also has an official Firebase plugin.
firebase.when: Firebase work from Gemini CLI, or when you prefer the CLI server over the plugin.

github.description: GitHub's remote MCP server (issues, PRs, repos, actions).
github.when: Repository automation beyond what the `gh` CLI covers.
